page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance deployed on KVM hypervisor infrastructure. Hardware resources include 8 dedicated vCPUs backed by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory is configured at 16.0 GB, providing an exact allocation of 2.0 GB per virtual core. This 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio aligns with compute-heavy deployment patterns where core availability takes precedence over large memory allocations.

The instance carries a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth rating, accommodating standard data transfer requirements between network nodes and attached storage systems. Local ephemeral storage is not included on the instance, requiring all persistence to be provisioned through remote network-attached block volumes. Furthermore, the server contains zero dedicated GPU accelerators. This lean resource profile eliminates hardware costs associated with high memory capacity or specialized graphics hardware, maximizing cost efficiency for core-centric compute execution.

Workload positioning for the ecs.c9a.2xlarge centers on processing tasks that require consistent CPU performance with moderate memory demands. Suitable deployment cases include build farm workers, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) execution nodes, web server layers, API gateways, and distributed compute worker nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core, offering high compute density for workloads that prioritize processor capacity over memory volume. The server lacks local storage, relying on external cloud block storage for persistence, and contains no GPU accelerators. Networking performance is established at a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The lean memory profile and dedicated CPU allocation offer a cost-effective hardware footprint for compute-intensive operations without paying for unused memory overhead. The instance is well-suited for batch processing, web application hosting, continuous integration pipelines, microservices, and general compute tasks.
